full_judgment: 15. Dr M Zahir, the learned Counsel appearing for the writ-petitioner respondent No. 1 in Civil Appeal No. 278 of 2003, has submitted that the recent trend is to interfere with the contract to see if the tender process or valuation thereof is transparent. With reference to Article 21 of the Constitution, he has submitted that a duty is cast on a citizen to protect public property inasmuch as to avoid the loss to the public exchequer. The learned Counsel has further submitted with reference to the decision in the case of ETV Ltd vs Dr Chowdhury Mahmood Hasan and others reported in 54 DLR (AD) 130 at page 144 that the cutting edge of law is remedial and the art of justice has to respond so that transparency wins over opaqueness which is the Constitutional obligation under Article 21 of the Constitution. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the bid of the writ-respondent No.4 being a conditional bid was not permitted under the bid terms inasmuch as the same was violative of the condition specified in section 111 regarding multiple contract of the categories 1,2 and 3.
